title: Fine Dust Warning
description:
Today's fine dust index: Very Bad.
The sky says so before the app notification even arrives. A grey haze.

China's yellow dust mixed with domestic exhaust, they say —
but who's really to blame is always a debate.

choices.text: KF94 mask on — go out as planned
choices.result_text:
Masked up and headed out. Stuffy breath, fogged glasses.

In this country, the mask is already a seasonal accessory.
Delivery riders, parcel workers — everyone's in KF94.

choices.text: Work from home — don't step outside at all
choices.result_text:
Drew the curtains and spent the day indoors.

Grey sky outside, quiet inside. Not bad at all.
Korea's weather sometimes gives you a legitimate excuse to stay in.

title: Cherry Blossom Week
description:
First week of April — the cherry blossoms explode.
Yeouido embankment, Seokchon Lake, Gyeongbokgung stone walls.

The petals last a week.
All of Seoul descends on that one week.

choices.text: Push through the crowds to see them
choices.result_text:
Shoulder to shoulder with strangers — but the pink was worth it.

A petal landed on your shoulder. You took a photo.
For that one week, the whole slog of Seoul spring becomes bearable.

choices.text: Just look at them in photos
choices.result_text:
Saw it on Instagram. Yeouido was all pink.

You'll go in person next year. You said the same thing last year.
Somewhere along the way, cherry blossoms became a 'next time' kind of season.

title: Monsoon Season
description:
July — the monsoon starts.
It's been raining for days. Looks like it'll stop. Then it rains more.

Convenience store umbrellas are sold out.
The goshiwon hallway smells of wet umbrellas.

choices.text: Use the monsoon — catch up on studying indoors
choices.result_text:
Not going out weather anyway. Opened a book.

The rain became white noise. I concentrated.
Days you hold the line in — they put you ahead on the sunny ones.

Picked up my phone, put it down. Picked it up again.

The monsoon doesn't drain your body — it drains your morale.
A few days without a single ray of sunlight and something sinks, for no clear reason.

title: Heat Wave
description:
August — feels like 40°C.
A notice is posted at the subway station: the AC is broken.

Asphalt heat outside, humidity inside.
The goshiwon room's AC has been making noise with no cold air since last night.

choices.text: Refuge in a café — buy air conditioning with a coffee
choices.result_text:
A wave of cold hit as you opened the café door. You stood in it for a moment.

Iced Americano, two hours. Six thousand won for AC.
But today, that was the whole plan — and it was enough.

choices.text: Public cooling shelter — the community center
choices.result_text:
The dong community center's cooling shelter. Elderly residents had claimed the good seats.

You sat quietly in a corner. Got a paper cup of iced barley tea.
Free air conditioning. You didn't know this service existed.

title: Cold Snap
description:
Minus 17°C. The weather service has issued an extreme cold warning.
The asphalt underfoot is frozen. Breath comes out white.

A Siberian air mass came down, they say.
Korea's winter doesn't explain itself — it just arrives.

choices.text: Spend the day at the jjimjilbang
choices.result_text:
Dipped my feet into the hot water and felt my whole body thaw.

Lay there in the sauna suit eating a steamed egg.
One of Seoul's survival secrets: 12,000 won buys you warmth, a shower, and somewhere to sleep.

choices.text: Survive on hobbang and fish cake at the convenience store
choices.result_text:
Stood in front of the convenience store's warming case for a while.
One steamed bun, one fish cake stick. Breath mixing with steam.

In a cold snap, the convenience store is a refuge.
Even with no money, you can stand somewhere warm for a moment.
